text:
leo: Heads up — noticed a surge of requests from EU paid customers being routed to us-east instead of eu-west for ~3m. Some of those got downgraded to the quantized-small variant and then bounced back to higher-tier, causing elevated latency.
serena: WTF, did routing policy respect customer_tier=gold? should have stayed in eu-west and used model_variant=prod-large.
matt: Seeing the same in traces. Smart router applied region_fallback=true when aux region was marked degraded, but the tier routing didn't pin model_variant. results: cross-region + variant downgrade + retry -> amplification.
ops-bot: alert: route-anomaly detected (id=R-2026-09-13-77) — cross-region spill to us-east, 46% of gold traffic, 00:03:20 window.
aya: Quick question — is this the canary we rolled last night that changed fallback precedence? I thought precedence was: tier routing -> model pinned -> region fallback.
leo: canary config probably changed precedence to prioritize capacity over tier, yes. Need to confirm.
jamie: grabbing the canary diff now.
jamie: diff snippet:
```
- fallback_order: [region, variant, capacity]
+ fallback_order: [capacity, region, variant]
```
serena: omg. that explains why premium got capacity-first and ended up in smaller quantized variants in other regions.
matt: Impact: latency spike for some SLAs and a handful of degraded responses; cost slightly lower but not acceptable.
devex: Any quick mitigation we can flip? Circuit-breaker at router level to prevent cross-region for Tier>=gold?
leo: yes. proposal: temp patch to canary -> set fallback_order back to [region, variant, capacity] and enable a hard rule: if customer_tier in (gold,enterprise) then region_routing_strict=true.
aya: I can flip the feature flag for the canary in ~2m.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback started for feature "smart-fallback-precedence" (canary) by aya @ 1779001271.
matt: after rollback, seeing route matrix stabilize. no more cross-region hits in last 30s.
serena: also recommend adding a circuit-breaker rule: if >5% of tier traffic crosses region within 1m, auto-open and route back to pinned region.
leo: agree. add to backlog: visual in Console -> per-tier cross-region heatmap + alerting. tagging devex for UX.
devex: noted — will mock a compact alert card for Console that shows tier, percent_cross_region, offending model_variant.
jamie: followup: we should add unit tests for fallback ordering and a property test that ensures pinning invariants for pinned models.
aya: postmortem: I'll write short incident note and link traces. rollcall: will add remediation steps and timeline.
leo: thanks all. tl;dr: canary changed fallback precedence -> cross-region routing for premium -> small-variant downgrades -> amplified latency. Rollback successful. Next: circuit-breaker + console telemetry + stronger canary gating.
serena: also file a quick RFC to make fallback_order explicit in rollout UI, not just a yaml blob.
leo: pinging security & sales to pre-empt any customer questions.
ops-bot: close: route-anomaly R-2026-09-13-77 (resolved) at 1779001299 :white_check_mark:
